title: End-to-End Inventory Prediction and Contract Allocation for Guaranteed Delivery Advertising

problem.claim: Guaranteed Delivery advertising requires allocating predicted advertising impression inventory to fulfill advance delivery contracts.

gap.claim: Prior work focused mainly on online serving, while traditional selling approaches separated inventory prediction from contract allocation, which can produce inferior allocation performance.

contributions.claim: The Neural Lagrangian Selling model jointly predicts impression inventory and optimizes contract allocation with a unified learning objective.
A differentiable Lagrangian layer enables backpropagation through the allocation problem and direct optimization of allocation regret.
A graph convolutional neural network extracts predictive features from the bipartite allocation graph to support optimization under varied targets and constraints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first study to apply end-to-end prediction and optimization to industrial Guaranteed Delivery selling problems.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved Guaranteed Delivery selling performance compared with existing two-stage approaches.
The authors report that the optimization layer outperforms baseline solvers in computational efficiency and solution quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: Guaranteed Delivery advertising supports advance contracts for targeted impression delivery.
Existing research and two-stage selling approaches leave a performance gap in contract allocation.
The paper introduces an end-to-end model with a differentiable Lagrangian layer and graph-based predictive features.
Experiments report improved selling performance and stronger solver efficiency and solution quality.
The authors position the work as the first industrial GD selling application of end-to-end prediction and optimization and suggest broader applicability.

source_observation.claim: Separating inventory prediction from contract allocation can lead to inferior allocation performance.

interpretation.claim: When prediction quality directly affects downstream decisions, jointly training prediction and optimization may reduce objective mismatch.

application.claim: Consider differentiable decision layers for forecasting-and-allocation workflows with explicit downstream objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that end-to-end optimization is preferable for every prediction and allocation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, experimental setup, or numerical results.
The abstract does not identify the baseline solvers or quantify computational and solution-quality improvements.
The abstract does not detail the allocation targets, constraints, or model architecture.
